loop.observation: Loop refresh dispatch can discover non-workflow refresh commands or all-stale command evidence sources that safe GitHub workflow dispatch cannot execute.
loop.hypothesis: Merging fresh command evidence sources, emitting ignored refresh commands as redacted closed-loop candidates with subjects, preserving command-level claim/evidence-chain scope in workflow dispatches, Actions summary/notice output, and ignored-command candidates, and converting all-stale inputs into source_stale candidates with stale-source subjects lets registry refresh commands and candidate-decision next commands share the same safe dispatch path without losing expired-evidence failures.
loop.execute: Generate a dispatch plan and optional candidate artifact from one or more loop-refresh command evidence files without shell-evaluating command strings, preserve stale source diagnostics as source_stale evidence when no fresh source remains, preserve refresh workflow claim/evidence-chain scope into each structured workflow dispatch and GitHub Actions summary/notice, preserve ignored target verifier claim/evidence-chain scope into the candidate subject, and verify the sample path with real closed-loop candidate decision command output.
loop.evaluate: The verifier fails on unsafe workflow command parsing, missing ignored command details, missing repeated command input coverage, missing candidate-decision producer coverage, missing workflow dispatch claim/evidence-chain scope, missing Actions summary/notice scope output, missing candidate subjects, missing ignored-command claim/evidence-chain scope, missing candidate source refs, missing stale-source candidate evidence, or missing adoption commands.
loop.retrospective: This keeps workflow dispatch safe while preventing workflow refresh intent, target verifier commands, claim/evidence-chain context, GitHub Actions visibility, or expired command evidence from either loop-registry or candidate-decision evidence from falling back into human memory.
